fields.System.Title: FDN-801 — Write events transactionally
fields.System.Description:
Story

As a developer, I want events written to a table inside the business transaction, so
that an event never describes something that did not happen, and a change never goes
unannounced.

Acceptance criteria

  • - Given a business change that publishes an event, then the event row is inserted in the
  • same transaction as the change.
  • - Given the transaction rolls back, then no event row exists.
  • - Given the transaction commits, then exactly one event row exists per published event.
  • - Given an event row, then it carries event_id, event_type, occurred_at,
  • aggregate_id, version, payload, and correlation_id.
  • - Given the service layer, then there is no code path that sends an event directly over
  • the network.

Traceability

| Aspect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Modules | platform |
| Tables | outbox |
| Risks | Event published before commit ([doc 09 §2.4](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md)); event lost after commit ([doc 08 §10](../../../docs/08-data-sync-and-migrations.md)) |
| Tests | unit · integration · rollback |
